fields.title: Learn more about Enact: Building an Open Source Repository for Practice Research - September 9th

content.value: The next
Apereo Foundation Microconference
features an exciting new project in our community:
Enact, a specialist practice research repository built using Hyku.
Register for free
to join on September 9, 2026 at 8:00 AM PT / 11:00 AM ET / 15:00 UTC
Practice research produces outputs that rarely fit the mold of the article or the dataset

: performances, exhibitions, compositions, installations, and the processes and narratives that give them meaning. Conventional institutional repositories were designed around text, so much of this work stays invisible. Enact is a specialist practice research repository funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC). A cross-institutional team, led from the University of Westminster and including Queen Mary University of London and the University of Leeds, is building it in the open for the international practice research community.

This session introduces the project and the thinking behind it, including the PR Voices metadata schema, a project-centred data model that captures process and context alongside outputs, and the Pathfinders programme that puts practice researchers and repository experts at the center of co-design. We'll show how the team is building Enact on the open-source Samvera Hyku platform, share what we've learned working across three organizations and an international user community, and talk about where other institutions can plug in.

Attendees will leave with:
An understanding of what practice research is and why its outputs challenge conventional repository infrastructure
A look at how the PR Voices metadata schema captures process, context, and the full range of contributors beyond a single author
A view into how the Pathfinder co-design programme, now including five Early Adopter institutions, shapes development priorities
Concrete ways to follow the project and get involved ahead of its Year 2 launch
Presenters
Nick Steinwachs, President, Notch8

. Nick leads Notch8, a Samvera Community partner that builds and hosts open-source repository infrastructure for universities, libraries, and cultural heritage organizations. Notch8 is the development partner on the Enact repository build.
Rory McNicholl, Digital Research Team Lead, CoSector, University of London
. Rory has spent two decades building services for research data and scholarly communication, and leads the CoSector team serving as Enact's technology partner.
Jenny Evans, Enact Project Lead, University of Westminster
. Jenny leads Enact: PR Voices and SPARKLE Phase 2, building on Westminster's pioneering work in practice research repositories and open research infrastructure.

fields.title: The Samvera Community joins the Apereo Foundation

content.value: The Samvera Community is excited to announce our new fiscal sponsor, the
Apereo Foundation

. The Apereo Foundation is a global nonprofit organization with over 25 years of experience advocating for open source software in higher education. They share our commitment to open, community-governed, and sustainable software communities.

The Samvera Community made this change with the full support of Samvera Partners as well as our previous fiscal sponsor, OASIS Open. This new sponsorship arrangement minimizes and simplifies our community overhead costs, ensuring we are maximizing the return on every dollar of contribution to the community.  Apereo will also provide new ways to engage with a broader community of academic open infrastructure.
Apereo is equally excited to learn from our community and the library open source ecosystem. You can
read their full welcome message on the Apereo website

The Samvera Community will continue to have the same governance structure, including an elected Board. The Community Bylaws will soon be updated to reflect the new fiscal sponsor and the changes will be voted on by Samvera Partners.

OASIS Open has been an invaluable resource to the Samvera Community and their support over the past five years has strengthened our governance and operations. We look forward to an equally cooperative relationship with the Apereo Foundation.
The Avalon Media System team is proud to announce release 8.2!

Avalon 8.2 includes improved object management with a revamped permissions model: Units are now full objects with their own staff and user permissions, and permissions are now inherited instead of per-object, making it easy to add read-only access to large collections for specific users and groups. 8.2 also includes support for Audio Description files, forced captions, and the latest version of the Ramp media component library.
Units and Permission Management
Units are now full objects where user roles and default access can be set
The "Manage" dashboard now allows for management of both Units and Collections
A new user role, Unit Admin, allows for ownership and access at the Unit level
Users are no longer required to be members of the "Managers" system group to be in a Manager role
Item permissions can be set on Units, to be inherited by child Collections
Items now inherit permissions directly from Collection values
Inherited permissions can be disabled for individual items in the Access Control edit page
Other Features and Changes
Accessibility criteria enforcement: a new configuration restricts items from being Published unless media files have associated captions or transcripts
Audio Description text track files can now be added to media files and enable an "AD" button in the media player
Donor Note field added to descriptive metadata
Updates to supplemental file naming for downloads on the item page
Legacy XML structure editor removed and replaced with a JSON-based editor in the Structure Metadata Editor tool
Improvements to oEmbed responses
Updates for automated UI tests with Cypress
Ramp 5.1
Support for Audio Description text tracks
Support for forced captions
Playback position is now saved in browser storage
Build system migrated to Vite
Added show more/less functionality to transcript cues
Player controls now display when Ramp encounters errors
New fallback strategy for source selection
Markers now sort chronologically on load
VideoJS now bundled in Ramp and no longer needs to be installed as a peer dependency
React upgrades: React 19 now required for Ramp
Bug Fixes
Improved error handling for object type mismatches
Fixed a bug causing unnecessary m3u8 calls
Timeliner updated to new build with bug fixes and accessibility fixes
See the Avalon wiki for
full upgrade instructions
and see GitHub for the
full changelog
